title: U.S. House · Illinois's 16th District
area: North-central Illinois, including Peoria, Bloomington-Normal, and the Quad Cities area.

context.text: Incumbent Darin LaHood ran essentially unopposed, winning the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 99.8% (write-in votes made up the remainder). Paul Nolley won the Democratic primary unopposed with 100% of the vote.

candidates.name: Darin LaHood
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 99.8% of the vote

summary.text: Darin LaHood is the Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 16th District. A Peoria native and former state and federal prosecutor, he served in the Illinois State Senate from 2011 to 2015 and was first elected to the U.S. House in a 2015 special election. He serves on the Ways and Means and Intelligence committees.

background.text: Born and raised in Peoria, Illinois, where his official biography calls him a third-generation Peorian; he graduated from Spalding High School. According to Wikipedia, he is the son of Ray LaHood, a former U.S. Representative for the district and U.S. Secretary of Transportation.
Earned a B.A. from Loras College and a J.D. from the University of Illinois-Chicago John Marshall Law School.

Spent more than nine years as a state and federal prosecutor, including as an Assistant State's Attorney in Cook and Tazewell counties and, from 2001 to 2006, as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in Las Vegas, Nevada, where he was selected as Chief Terrorism Prosecutor.
Practiced with the Peoria law firm Miller, Hall & Triggs from 2006 until his election to the House.
Ran unsuccessfully for Peoria County State's Attorney in 2008, then was appointed to the Illinois State Senate in February 2011 and won a full term in 2012, serving until 2015.

Won a 2015 special election to the U.S. House and was sworn in on September 17, 2015. He represented the 18th District from 2015 to 2023 and, after redistricting, the 16th District; he was most recently re-elected November 5, 2024.

Joined the House Ways and Means Committee in January 2018, chairs its Work and Welfare Subcommittee and sits on the Trade Subcommittee; he was appointed to the House Intelligence Committee in March 2021 and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party in January 2022.

Co-chairs the bipartisan U.S.-China Working Group, Digital Trade Caucus, U.S.-Lebanon Friendship Caucus and Congressional Soccer Caucus. His official biography says he lives in Peoria with his wife Kristen and their three sons, and has completed five marathons.

priorities.text: Our state and our nation needs a jobs revival, but the employment landscape won't change if crippling policies do not. I believe it is the government's responsibility to create an atmosphere where businesses can thrive. To get there, we need to cut overreaching regulations, eliminate burdensome mandates, and reform and simplify the tax code by closing loopholes and cutting rates.

In Central Illinois, our farmers work tirelessly to provide for our families in Illinois as well as our country and nations abroad. To fully support the agriculture community, we must maintain effective programs that allow our farmers to remain globally competitive, we must reduce regulations, and we must expand opportunities for trade.

Trade is of paramount importance to the economy of the 16th Congressional district. In order to continue to facilitate trade that benefits American workers, I believe it is essential to strengthen dialogue with our trade partners, to have clear agreements, and enforceable free and fair trade laws.

positions.summary: Says the U.S. must secure the southern border and enforce immigration laws.
positions.quote: However, the American rule of law must be respected, especially among those who hope to live here. We need to secure our southern border and enforce our immigration laws.

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-life and says he will continue to advocate in Congress for protecting life and the rights of the unborn from conception.
positions.quote: I firmly believe that we must stand up and protect the sanctity of life from the moment of conception on. I will continue to serve as a proud and active advocate in Congress for protecting life and preserving the rights of the unborn.

positions.summary: Says he strongly supports the Second Amendment and will work to defend hunters, sportsmen, and firearm owners.
positions.quote: I strongly support the Second Amendment and in Congress I will fight to defend the hunters, sportsmen, and firearm owners of Central and West Central Illinois.

positions.summary: Says his priority is to repeal components of the Affordable Care Act and move toward a patient-centered, market-based healthcare system rather than expanded government coverage.
positions.quote: In Congress, my priority is to repeal the damaging components of Obamacare and work towards a patient—centered efficient and effective health care system.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party; the Committee on Ways and Means (chairs the Work and Welfare subcommittee); and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (vice chair, Central Intelligence Agency subcommittee; chair, National Security Agency and Cyber subcommittee).

candidates.name: Paul Nolley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Paul Nolley is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 16th Congressional District. A Rockford native, he began his career working on a state senator's campaign, then worked with community organizations before becoming executive director of Project First Rate, which advocates for union contractors and tradespeople. He was unopposed in the March 2026 Democratic primary.

background.text: Born in Rockford, Illinois, and attended Illinois State University.
Describes a working-class upbringing: his father was a mechanic and his mother worked several jobs, neither with a college education, and he held blue-collar jobs in restaurants and on farms.
After college he worked on State Sen. Steve Stadelman's 2012 campaign, then for community organizations including the YMCA, United Way and Habitat for Humanity.
Is executive director of Project First Rate, described by NPR Illinois / WNIJ as an organization advocating for union contractors and tradespeople.
Advanced from the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed, with 38,665 votes.

sources.title: A Rockford Democrat wants to offer a different vision in Illinois’ 16th Congressional District

researchNotes: LaHood's positions and priorities are drawn from his official House issues pages. No campaign website or citable public statements were found for Paul Nolley beyond basic biographical facts. Nolley's biography rests on Ballotpedia and a May 2025 NPR Illinois / WNIJ profile; no campaign website was found, and no prior elected office was identified.
